description: Argument injection without a shell. Three positives pin direct list augmentation, shlex.split and str.split: each can create a dash-leading argv element, and checking only the final shlex result does not validate its siblings. Two negatives pin the exceptions the rule can prove from the vector itself: a literal -- before the caller's element, and removing every leading dash from that element.

expected.note: a username can become a useradd option through list augmentation
shlex.split creates several arguments; validating only parts[-1] says nothing about the preceding elements
str.split creates several independently interpreted arguments too
